subject: chemistry
title: Natural polymers: amino acids, proteins and DNA
key_idea: (Separate science) Many polymers are made by living things. Proteins are polymers of amino acids, DNA is a polymer of four nucleotides, and starch and cellulose are polymers of sugars such as glucose.

blocks.text: Proteins are polymers made from amino acids. The amino acids are the monomers.

items.meaning: (AQA: Higher tier) A molecule with two different functional groups: an amino group, –NH₂, and a carboxyl group, –COOH.
(AQA: Higher tier) A polymer made when amino acids join by condensation polymerisation.
A polymer made from amino acids.

items: (AQA: Higher tier) Amino acids have two different functional groups in one molecule.
(AQA: Higher tier) They react by condensation polymerisation to make polypeptides, losing water.
(AQA: Higher tier) Different amino acids can be combined in the same chain to make proteins.

blocks.label: (AQA: Higher tier) Glycine making a polypeptide
where: H₂NCH₂COOH is glycine, an amino acid.
[–NHCH₂CO–] is the repeating unit of the polypeptide.
n is a large number, with no unit.

items: Proteins are polymers based on amino acids.
(AQA: Higher tier) Amino acids have two different functional groups and join by condensation polymerisation.

blocks.text: DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) is a large molecule essential for life. It encodes the genetic instructions for the development and functioning of living organisms and viruses.

items.meaning: One of the four different monomers that make up DNA.
The shape of DNA: two polymer chains twisted together.

items: Most DNA molecules are two polymer chains.
The chains are made from four different monomers called nucleotides.
The two chains are in the form of a double helix.
DNA is a polymer made from four different monomers called nucleotides.
Most DNA molecules are two chains in a double helix.

blocks.text: Starch and cellulose are naturally occurring polymers that are important for life. Both are polymers based on sugars, such as glucose.

diagram.alt: Sort each natural polymer or description by its monomer.
diagram.prompt: Sort each item by the monomer it is made from.

items.text: Polymer with a double helix shape

items: Starch and cellulose are polymers of sugars, such as glucose.
DNA is made from nucleotides, proteins from amino acids, and starch and cellulose from glucose.

checks.q: Name the monomers that make up DNA, proteins and starch.
checks.a: DNA: nucleotides. Proteins: amino acids. Starch: sugars (glucose).

checks.q: Describe the shape and structure of DNA.
checks.a: Two polymer chains in a double helix, made from four different monomers (nucleotides).

checks.q: Name two naturally occurring polymers made from glucose.

worked_example.question:
Glucose is produced when algae photosynthesise.

Name two naturally occurring polymers produced from glucose.

Many biological substances are polymers.

Complete the table to state the type of monomer which forms each of the biological polymers.

Polymer | Type of monomer
DNA | ______
Protein | ______
Starch | ______
answer_points: DNA: nucleotides (named nucleotides such as adenine, thymine, cytosine and guanine are allowed).
Starch: sugars (glucose or monosaccharide is allowed).
worked_example.tip: One mark for each correct monomer.

worked_example.question:
Naturally occurring polyamides are found in food.

Name the type of monomer which forms naturally occurring polyamides.

blocks.text: (Supplement) Proteins are natural polyamides. They are made from amino acid monomers.

items.meaning: A monomer with the general structure H₂N–CHR–COOH, where R is a side chain that differs between amino acids.

blocks.text: (Supplement) A protein is drawn as –NH–□–CO–NH–□–CO–NH–□–CO–, where each box is a different amino acid unit.
